description: Owned US-PR-016 real cross-version Agent/SQLite upgrade and rollback closure. New owner assets only; never runs the shared Docker lifecycle fixture, the old 8443/8445 stacks or a remote host.

env.PANEL_TEST_DATABASE_URL: owned PostgreSQL 17 on 127.0.0.1 with a database name prefixed dp_owned_; the runner creates it itself
env.PP_DEMO_UPGRADE_OLD_AGENT: old Agent binary built read-only from a historical commit with `git archive` (default 52bf44a); the saved build/linux-amd64/agent artifact is only accepted via --old-agent and its provenance is recorded as UNKNOWN
env.PP_DEMO_UPGRADE_NEW_AGENT: new Agent binary built from the current worktree candidate
env.PP_DEMO_UPGRADE_OLD_CORE: official Xray v26.3.23 binary with geoip.dat/geosite.dat from the same release
env.PP_DEMO_UPGRADE_NEW_CORE: official Xray v26.3.27 binary with geoip.dat/geosite.dat from the same release
env.PP_DEMO_UPGRADE_STATE_DIR: optional absolute 0700 state/evidence directory; never committed
env.PP_DEMO_UPGRADE_PROBE_CORE: independent staged copy of one official Xray release, used only as the traffic client so the managed core under test is never also the client

does_not: touch 127.0.0.1:8443, 8445, Agent-lab, the shared 15432 database, .devdb or any remote host
reuse deploy/docker-lifecycle.sh or any shared Docker/SSH fixture
change production code, SQL, migrations, the shared runner or another owner's tests
rewrite the Agent SQLite queue directly, clear it, or accept a version string as the switch proof
notes: Old-source provenance: the old Agent is built from an explicit commit with `git archive` in a private dir; the receipt records commit, archive sha, go SDK, go.mod/go.sum sha, requires, build command and binary sha. The shipped build/linux-amd64/agent cannot be attributed to 52bf44a: its .proxypanel-build records no commit, its buildinfo pins golang.org/x/sys v0.36.0 while 52bf44a pins v0.47.0 (only the initial ec7ee10 used v0.36.0), and the sibling SHA256SUMS is a same-directory integrity anchor, not provenance.
Both known Agent commits label themselves 0.1.1, so the proof uses binary sha256 + a heartbeat newer than the pre-action snapshot + the reported core version.

Core switching is proven per step by the Agent-owned pid record: managed core pid, /proc starttime, exe path, exe sha256 against the expected official binary sha, owner uid, cgroup and config-under-state-dir, plus a real fixed-body transfer through that core with a stage-independent client core and a never-revoked control member. The core pid must change on switch/rollback and every stage writes raw per-step JSON.
The old Agent's own SQLite state is the upgrade input; the case refuses an unmerged WAL or unknown table layout and never repairs it.
The retained outbox must be credited once per batch id with the identical payload sha256; a revoked member must stay revoked (403) while the control member stays served.
Technical rollback uses the old binary on the upgraded state; restoring an old database dump to regain access is explicitly not used.

Cleanup stops the owned PostgreSQL with pg_ctl -m fast before any recovery sweep, records pg_ctl/exit status and postgres_graceful separately from SIGKILL recovery, and takes an after process+TCP/UDP listener snapshot compared by exact pid/starttime/exe identity.
